messages.text: 'It wasn't good enough' - Hamilton reveals 'huge' talks over Ferrari blunder

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton has revealed Ferrari held a "huge discussion" to reflect on a strategic error at the Bahrain Grand Prix that he says "wasn't good enough".
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver says team held 'huge discussions' over strategy following Bahrain GP tyre-choice blunder | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver says team held 'huge discussions' over strategy following Bahrain GP tyre-choice blunder Lewis Hamilton plummeted from second on the grid after starting last weekend's Bahrain GP on slick dry tyres in wet conditions; watch Practice at 9.30am followed by Sprint Qualifying at 1.30pm on Friday live on Sky Sports F1 as the Singapore Grand Prix weekend begins Thursday 8 October 2026 15:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following criticisms at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Lewis Hamilton defends Ferrari strategists Lewis Hamilton has revealed Ferrari held a "huge discussion" to reflect on a strategic error at the Bahrain Grand Prix that he says "wasn't good enough". Ferrari fitted both Hamilton and his team-mate Charles Leclerc with slick dry tyres at last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix, which was being hosted in Malaysia and started on a wet track that the Italian squad anticipated would quickly dry out once the race began. The decision was proven wrong as Hamilton fell from his starting position of second to almost the back of the field in the opening stages, with the 14 of 22 drivers that started on the intermediate tyre gaining a huge advantage. metadata.summary: When Aston Villa went 1-0 up in north London, it felt inevitable that Tottenham would head into the international break winless in the Premier League.
metadata.content: Tottenham Sky Sports special podcast: Tim Sherwood and Michael Bridge assess Spurs' problems after winless start | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Tottenham Sky Sports special podcast: Tim Sherwood and Michael Bridge assess Spurs' problems after winless start In a special Sky Sports Spurs podcast, Tim Sherwood and Sky Sports News' Tottenham reporter Michael Bridge assess the club's winless start to the Premier League season, which has left them bottom; watch Man Utd vs Spurs on Saturday, live on Sky Sports; kick-off 5.30pm Declan Olley Football Journalist @declanolley Thursday 8 October 2026 11:21, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tim Sherwood and Michael Bridge believe Roberto De Zerbi is not under pressure despite their poor start to the season When Aston Villa went 1-0 up in north London, it felt inevitable that Tottenham would head into the international break winless in the Premier League. Last month's 3-2 home loss to Villa was the 47th game in this dismal run (D11 L36). "It is a worry, certainly at home because that's where you need the minerals," former Tottenham boss Tim Sherwood told a special Sky Sports Spurs podcast. messages.text: FIA introducing measures to avoid ‘software bug’ chaos repeat

metadata.summary: The FIA will introduce further changes to wet-weather engine software from the United States Grand Prix after completing a review into the "software bug" that further delayed the start of last week's rain-hit race in Malaysia.
metadata.content: FIA reveals Bahrain GP 'software bug' findings and planned changes after glitch caused issues before rain-hit Malaysia race | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content FIA reveals Bahrain GP 'software bug' findings and planned changes after glitch caused issues before rain-hit Malaysia race Same engine software fix introduced in Malaysia remains in place for Singapore in event of any wet weather; further update to follow for next round in USA; watch Practice at 9.30am followed by Sprint Qualifying at 1.30pm on Friday live on Sky Sports F1 at the Singapore GP Thursday 8 October 2026 11:38, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chaotic formation lap halts race start at Bahrain GP in Malaysia The FIA will introduce further changes to wet-weather engine software from the United States Grand Prix after completing a review into the "software bug" that further delayed the start of last week's rain-hit race in Malaysia. Several cars slowed or briefly stopped on the rain-hit laps to the grid last Sunday due to what the governing body after the race described as an "unprecedented combination" related to both the slow speed the cars were travelling in the wet and the sector configuration of the Sepang lap. The start procedure was abandoned and the Grand Prix eventually started 48 minutes later after a software update was issued by the FIA to all teams and power-unit manufacturers. messages.text: Pettersen bounces back on LET return as England's Humphreys moves second

metadata.summary: Suzann Pettersen marked her first round on the Ladies European Tour in four years with an even-par 72 at the Aramco Korea Championship as England's Lily May Humphreys earned a share of second place.
metadata.content: Aramco Korea Championship: Suzann Pettersen shoots even par in first round on Ladies European Tour after four years | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Aramco Korea Championship: Suzann Pettersen shoots even par in first round on Ladies European Tour after four years Suzann Pettersen makes return to Ladies European Tour for first time since 2022 and rallies after early dropped shots to card even-par 72, including monster birdie at 15; England's Lily May Humphreys in share of second after five-under 67; watch second round from 5.30am Friday Thursday 8 October 2026 12:21, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Suzann Petersen sank a huge birdie putt on the 15th at the Aramco Korea Championship, her first tournament since 2022 Suzann Pettersen marked her first round on the Ladies European Tour in four years with an even-par 72 at the Aramco Korea Championship as England's Lily May Humphreys earned a share of second place. Pettersen, 45, retired after sinking the winning putt for Team Europe in the 2019 Solheim Cup at Gleneagles, with her only appearance since the 2022 Aramco Team Series event in Jeddah. The Norwegian - who captained Europe at the 2023 and 2024 Solheim Cups - was three over after six holes in South Korea, bogeying the third and double bogeying the sixth.
